page.layout: One page of text, no margin notes. Top: printed page number at upper right. Below: a floral woodcut ornament, then a centred title in capitals and spaced type (three lines), then a centred italic heading, then a paragraph opening with a large woodcut initial L, set in verse lines.

main_text.head: EPIGRAMMATA EX BVCHANANO DE SVMPTA, ET NVNC PRIMVM edita.
IN POLYONYMVM.
main_text.p: LVsitanicus vnus es mare vltra, & Citra Agarbicus, Indicúsque, Arábsq; Perficus, Gineúsque, & Africanus, Congúsque, & Manicongus, & Zalofus,
Nec tuis titulis abest superbis Æthiops nimio perustus ęstu, Nec circum triplicem refusus orbem Cunctarum Oceanus parens aquarum.
Nec portus, neque merx, nec infula vlla est, Lucelli vnde leuis refulget aura, Quæ te non titulo augeat. Tot ergo Cui sunt nomina nónne iure regem Multis nominibus vocabo magnum?
Sed rex nominibus tot ille magnis Si belli furor, aut mare æstuosum Ccludat piperariam tabernam, Versuram faciet, vel esuribit.

page.notes: The initial L is a large woodcut letter, transcribed as L joined to the first word "Lusitanicus" (printed "Vsitanicus"; the initial letter stands in place of the L). Words in the first verse of the poem: the printer's spelling is kept. Possible printing errors: "Ccludat" (for Occludat) and "Versuram" and "esuribit" are kept as printed. Some letters in the scan are faint, particularly "Lucelli" and "Quæ te" line. Lines of verse have been transcribed as printed stanzas; a few words may be uncertain: "Gineúsque", "Congúsque" and "Arábsq;" are kept as printed. The running head and catchword are absent. Ornament at the top and the faint show-through text on the page are not transcribed.
